name: Paul-Heinz Wesjohann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Paul-Heinz Wesjohann is the chairman and namesake of Germany-based PHW Group, with more than $4 billion in annual sales.
PHW is the owner of Wiesenhof, which is the largest poultry processor in Germany. Overall the group employs 7,000 across Europe.
The firm also manufactures plant-based products for brands including Beyond Meat and Livekindly in Europe.
PHW Group was founded in 1999, when Wesjohann and his brother Erich decided to split up their family chicken company, originally dating to 1932.

name: Panagiotis Tsakos
forbes_bio: Panagiotis Tsakos is the founder of Tsakos Group, an Athens-based shipping company that owns more than 110 oil tankers, LNG vessels, container ships and dry cargo vessels.
Born on the island of Chios in a family of seafarers, he started the business in 1970. His son Nikolas joined the family firm in the mid-1980s.
In 1993, Nikolas set up tanker firm Tsakos Energy Navigation. One of the first tanker firms to go public, Nikolas listed it on the Oslo stock exchange in 1993 and in New York in 2002.
Nikolas has served as president and CEO of Tsakos Energy Navigation since 1993 and now runs the business, which he owns along with his father Panagiotis.
Panagiotis and Nikolas also own other investments including a mineral water brand, renewable energy projects, forestry, real estate and a stake in a Greek bank.
forbes_facts: In 2010, Tsakos founded the Maria Tsakos Foundation, named after his late daughter Maria, to focus on education, maritime traditions and environmental protection.
The foundation runs schools in the Greek island of Chios, Ghana and south America.

name: Tali Griffel
forbes_bio: Tali Griffel is the daughter of the late Menahem Gurevitch, who was longtime chairman and controlling shareholder of Menora Mivtachim, one of Israel's largest insurance and financial services groups.
Founded in 1935, Menora Mivtachim manages more than ILS 375 billion and is one of the country's largest institutional financial players.
Tali and her sister, Niva Gurevitch, inherited their father's controlling stake after his passing in 2013.
Each sister owns about ⅓ of the company, which has paid then more than $300 million dividends since 2014. Tali's husband, Eran Griffel, is chairman of Menora Mivtachim.

name: Amy Adams Strunk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Adams Strunk is controlling owner of the National Football League's Tennessee Titans. She gained control in 2015 following a family scrum.
In 2016, Adams Strunk was appointed to the NFL's Hall of Fame Committee and subsequently named to the Board of Trustees for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Adams Strunk inherited a share of the Titans from her father, Bud Adams, who founded the team as the Houston Oilers, after his death in 2013.
Before taking control of the team, she had spent time as owner of a few of the family's car dealerships and oil interests, and raising horses
In 2022, Adams Strunk reached agreement with the city of Nashville to build a new enclosed stadium for the Titans at a cost of $2.1 billion.

name: Andrey Andreev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Russian entrepreneur Andrey Andreev has built five online dating sites and apps since 2004: Mamba, Badoo, Bumble, Chappy and Lumen.
His most successful app in the U.S. by far is Bumble, cofounded with Whitney Wolfe Herd, which only allows female users to make the first reach-out.
In 2019, Andreev sold his majority stake in Bumble and Badoo to Blackstone Group in a deal that valued the sites at $3 billion.
In 2020, Andreev launched Stereo, an audio-only social media platform that competes with Clubhouse, another audio app.
Andreev got his start in the 1990s building and selling several startups including SpyLog, which tracked visitors to websites.
forbes_facts: As a weekend hobby, Andreev would sometimes cook alongside head chef Olivier Limousin at two-Michelin-star London restaurant L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon.

name: Bennett Dorrance
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: The grandson of John T. Dorrance, the inventor of condensed soup, Bennett Dorrance owns a 15% stake in Campbell Soup.
Dorrance retired from the Campbell's board in 2022, ending a 33 year stint.
Dorrance is a founding partner of DMB Associates, a real estate development firm with projects in Arizona, California and Hawaii.
A licensed pilot, Dorrance owns a private hangar in Scottsdale, Arizona that sometimes houses his vintage car collection.
The Dorrance Scholarship, established by Bennett and Jacquelynn Dorrance in 1999, has supported 150-plus first-generation college students in Arizona.

name: Nicola Leibinger-Kammueller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Nicola Leibinger-Kammueller owns 29.4% of the world's largest manufacturer of machine tools, TRUMPF, and serves as CEO.
The company traces its roots to 1923 when Christian Trumpf acquired a machine shop in Stuttgart.
Nicola's father, Berthold Leibinger, joined the company in 1961 and developed the first contour "nibbling" machine tool with numerical control.
Christian Trumpf, who had no children, chose Berthold as his successor and handed over control of the company to him in 1972.
After retiring from management in 2005, Berthold passed the company's ownership to his three children.
forbes_facts: Nicola, in addition to being active in various scientific, cultural and social institutions, is a board member at Siemens AG and Axel Springer SE.
Her brother, Peter, and sister, Regine, also each own 29.4% of Trumpf.

name: Edwin Leong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Edwin Leong is the sixth son of Henry G. Leong, a comprador of British trading house Jardine Matheson, who died when Edwin was just nine years old.
Leong earned the moniker "King of Shops" from amassing an immense portfolio of retail and commercial properties through Tai Hung Fai Enterprise.
Leong also ventured into the mass residential market during the pandemic.
He is the founder of the Tai Hung Fai Charitable Foundation, which focuses on helping needy children and the elderly.

name: Christine Knauf
forbes_bio: Christine Brigitte Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
forbes_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Eugene Kaspersky
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Eugene Kaspersky graduated from the Higher School of KGB and began creating his first antiviral programs in the early 1990s.
Kaspersky became interested in computer security in 1989 when his computer was infected with the 'Cascade' virus.
The young engineer founded Kaspersky Lab in 1997 and headed up the company's antivirus research.
Over 400 million users now use Kaspersky Lab products to protect their computers.
In 2019-2024 Kaspersky Lab bought about 70% of New Cloud Technologies, developer of office software suite MyOffice.
forbes_facts: President Trump signed a law that banned the use of Kaspersky Lab products within the U.S. government  due to concerns that it was vulnerable to Kremlin influence.

name: Nick Molnar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Nick Molnar cofounded Australian fintech startup Afterpay in 2015, which lets people pay for small items like dresses in 4 interest-free installments.
Before Afterpay, he had been Australia's top seller of jewelry on eBay, shipping thousands of packages a day.
Molar took his company public in April 2016, listing it on the Australian Stock Exchange; shares surged in 2020 during the pandemic but started declining on looming regulations.
U.S. payments firm Square acquired Afterpay for $29 billion in stock.  It was relisted as Block Inc.
forbes_facts: In March 2020, Afterpay agreed to pay $1 million to California regulators, who accused it of running an unlicensed lending business.
In response to the $1 million payment, Afterpay said in a statement, "Afterpay rejects the view that the Company operated illegally."
